name: Pellmouth
basis: Original setting written for Prospero Dungeon: a 1920s New England town with a cosmic-horror lean, modeled on real Massachusetts river and harbor towns. Nothing is taken from Lovecraft's stories or later works.
summary: A fog-bound town of about eighteen thousand people at the mouth of the Pell River on the North Shore of Massachusetts, 1926: a harbor and cannery, a shut-mouthed fishing quarter, a hill of gambrel roofs and a meetinghouse sealed for thirty years, a small university with a strange bequest, shoe mills, a flooded quarry, an asylum on the bluff and a lighthouse that keeps its own hours.

curated-2026-10.title: Pellmouth, Massachusetts, written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: An invented town. Its institutions, trades, prices and yearly calendar follow what was usual in North Shore harbor, shoe-mill, quarry and college towns of the mid-1920s, drawn from general historical knowledge. Every business, family and person named is fictional, and the legends and rumours are written for it; none is taken from Lovecraft or any later work. Rents are monthly, in 1926 dollars. Coordinates sit on the Essex County coast for distance estimates only; the climate follows that coast.

neighborhoods.name: Market Square
neighborhoods.summary: The brick and granite downtown around the old market house: the town hall, the bank, the Courier office, dry goods, the Bijou, the Athenaeum and the Boston & Maine depot at the foot of Depot Street.

neighborhoods.name: Harbor Front
neighborhoods.summary: Granite wharves, fish piers, the cannery, the Custom House and the ferry slip; it smells of tar, cod and coal smoke, and the fog horn on the point sets the rhythm of the night.

neighborhoods.name: The Narrows
neighborhoods.summary: The old fishing quarter where the river pinches in: leaning clapboard houses, net lofts and a Portuguese parish. Families have fished here for generations, marry among themselves and keep their own counsel; strangers are polite to and not much more.

neighborhoods.name: Meetinghouse Hill
neighborhoods.summary: A steep hill of gambrel-roofed captains' houses from the 1700s, elms, iron fences and slate gravestones, with the First Parish church, the Historical Society and the boarded-up Second Parish meetinghouse at the top.

neighborhoods.name: College Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Haskett University's brick halls and elm-shaded yard, the State Normal School, faculty houses, student rooming houses, the College Spa and the boathouse on the river below.

neighborhoods.name: Lower Falls
neighborhoods.summary: The shoe mills and their brick housing along the falls of the Pell, where French-Canadian families came down from Quebec to work; church bells, mill whistles and pork pies.

neighborhoods.name: South End
neighborhoods.summary: Triple-deckers, corner stores and an Irish parish south of Market Square, with the car barn, the YMCA, the ballfield and the Spiritualist hall where messages from the dead are read out on Sunday evenings.

neighborhoods.name: The Bluff
neighborhoods.summary: High ground north of the river mouth: the long brick wings of the State Hospital, its farm and greenhouses, a cliff walk above the rocks, and a few houses for hospital staff.

neighborhoods.name: Gannet Point
neighborhoods.summary: The rocky point at the harbor entrance with the lighthouse, the Coast Guard station, a long beach, the summer dance pavilion and shingled cottages that stand empty from October to June.

neighborhoods.name: Quarry Village
neighborhoods.summary: The granite company's village west of town: Italian, Polish and Finnish quarry families, a cooperative store, two halls, and the old pits, some of them flooded to a depth nobody has measured.

neighborhoods.name: West Parish
neighborhoods.summary: Farms, orchards and stone walls up the river: a grange hall, a cider mill, Pratt's Pond where the town skates, and Sayer's Rock, where a widow was examined for witchcraft in 1692.

transit.name: On foot
transit.summary: The town is small and steep: Market Square to the wharves is five minutes, to College Hill fifteen uphill. In fog people walk by the sound of the bell buoy.

transit.name: Pellmouth & Shore Street Railway
transit.summary: Yellow trolley cars every fifteen minutes from the South End car barn through Market Square to College Hill and the Lower Falls, and out the shore line to the Bluff; a dime a ride.

transit.name: Boston & Maine Railroad
transit.summary: Steam trains from the Depot Street station to Boston in about an hour and a quarter, and north along the coast; the evening train brings the papers.

transit.name: Pell River ferry
transit.summary: A small steam ferry from the Harbor Front slip to the Narrows landing and on to Gannet Point, every half hour in summer and four times a day in winter; it does not run in thick fog.

transit.name: Shore Road motor bus
transit.summary: Motor buses from Market Square out to Gannet Point, the State Hospital, Quarry Village and West Parish, where the trolley does not go.

places.name: Market Square
places.summary: The cobbled square around the 1790s market house, with the town pump, the war memorial and a bench where the same old-timers watch the weather and everybody else.

places.name: Kimball's Lunch
places.summary: A narrow lunch counter of twelve stools: fish chowder, hash, pie and coffee, with the Courier's reporters at one end and the bank clerks at the other.

places.name: Tarbox's Drug Store soda fountain
places.summary: A marble soda fountain at the back of the drug store: frappes, ice cream sodas, coffee and a newspaper rack; couples come after the pictures.

places.name: Abbot's Chop House
places.summary: Dark panelling, mutton chops, broiled scrod and Indian pudding, where the selectmen lunch and anyone with something to celebrate dines.

places.name: Larkin & Pratt Dry Goods
places.summary: Three floors of dry goods, ready-made dresses, oilskins and wool, with cash carriers whizzing on wires to the office upstairs.

places.name: Tuttle's Antiquarian Books
places.summary: A crooked shop of secondhand books, sea charts and town histories, with a back room of older things the owner shows only to buyers they know.

places.name: Bijou Theatre
places.summary: Pictures with an organist, vaudeville on Saturdays and amateur nights; the balcony is where the town does its courting.

places.name: Pellmouth Athenaeum
places.summary: A subscription library of leather armchairs, ships' portraits and bound newspapers back to 1790, with a reading room open to anyone who keeps quiet.

places.name: Boston & Maine depot
places.summary: The brick depot with its iron canopy, where the Boston papers come in on the evening train and the town meets whoever is coming home.

places.name: Central Wharf and fish pier
places.summary: The granite fish pier where the schooners and the new motor draggers unload cod, haddock and mackerel before dawn, and gulls argue over everything.

places.name: Old Custom House
places.summary: A granite custom house with an eagle over the door; the harbormaster posts the week's tide table on the board outside, and people in the Narrows read it and then do as they please.

places.name: Driscoll's Oyster Bar
places.summary: A long marble counter of oysters, steamers and fish chowder under a pressed-tin ceiling; the coffee comes with a nod toward the back stairs.

places.name: The Night Boat Diner
places.summary: A dining car set down by the ferry slip, open all night for cannery shifts and fishing crews: fried eggs, beans, coffee and doughnuts at a nickel.

places.name: The Ropewalk
places.summary: A speakeasy in the long loft of an old ropewalk, reached through a sail-maker's shop: Canadian whisky that came in on a foggy night, a piano, a three-piece band and a knock you have to know.

places.name: Seamen's Bethel
places.summary: A plain chapel for sailors with boards on the walls naming every Pellmouth vessel lost since 1716 and everyone aboard; people stop in on the way to the wharf.

places.name: Hapgood's Ship Chandlery
places.summary: Rope, oilskins, lamp oil, compasses and a wall of barometers that the old skippers tap on their way past.

places.name: Ellsworth's boatyard
places.summary: A boatyard of sheds and slipways where dories and draggers are built and mended, smelling of oakum, pine tar and steam boxes.

places.name: Church of the Holy Ghost
places.summary: The Portuguese parish church, white clapboard with a blue door, where the fleet is blessed in June and the old keep candles burning for those at sea.

places.name: Medeiros' Lunch
places.summary: Four tables in a front room: kale soup, fish stew, linguiça and bread, and a silence when a stranger walks in that lifts once they have ordered.

places.name: Furtado's Bakery
places.summary: Sweet bread, malassadas on Tuesdays and strong coffee from five in the morning, when the fishing crews come in for the day's bread.

places.name: Narrows fish market
places.summary: Open stalls along the landing of salt cod, fresh flounder, clams and eels, sold by families who will tell you the fish but not where they caught it.

places.name: Cordage Lane net lofts
places.summary: Weathered lofts where nets are mended by hand and hung to dry; the menders sing in Portuguese and stop when the tide turns.

places.name: The tide steps
places.summary: Worn granite steps running down into the river at the end of Water Lane; on the big spring tides the water comes up to the top step, and the Narrows lights a lamp in every window that faces it.

places.name: Rapoza's variety store
places.summary: A dim little store of thread, candles, holy pictures, tobacco and penny candy, where the Narrows leaves messages for one another behind the counter.

places.name: The old Second Parish meetinghouse
places.summary: A tall white meetinghouse boarded and chained since 1894. The town record says the congregation split and the roof failed; nobody has paid to mend it, and nobody will buy it.

places.name: Old Hill Burying Ground
places.summary: Slate stones with winged skulls and weeping willows under old elms; a quiet walk with a view of the harbor, and the sexton's lantern after dark.

places.name: Pellmouth Historical Society
places.summary: A 1720s house of portraits, ship models, samplers and the county court papers of 1692, which the volunteers will show you but would rather not discuss.

places.name: The Gambrel Tea Room
places.summary: Tea, scones, chicken salad and lemon cake in the front parlours of an old house, among the hill's garden clubs and faculty spouses.

places.name: First Parish Church
places.summary: The white Unitarian church with the town clock in its steeple, where the old families sit in the same box pews their great-grandparents bought.

places.name: Wainwright House garden
places.summary: A walled eighteenth-century garden of box hedges, roses and a sundial, opened to visitors by the Garden Club on afternoons in season.

places.name: Merrill Street antiques
places.summary: A parlour shop of pewter, sea chests, samplers and portraits of nobody in particular, sold off by families letting go of the old houses one room at a time.

places.name: Haskett University Old Yard
places.summary: A green of elms and red brick halls from the 1780s on, with a chapel bell that rings the hours and students lying on the grass in May.

places.name: Lindall Library and the Whitcomb Room
places.summary: The university library, open to townspeople by card. Its Whitcomb Room keeps a family bequest of almanacs, sermons, ships' logs and private journals that may not leave the room, and by the terms of the gift is locked at sundown.

places.name: Haskett Museum of Natural History
places.summary: Cases of birds, shells, whale bones and things brought home by Pellmouth captains, some labelled only "Pacific, before 1840".

places.name: The College Spa
places.summary: A corner spa of tonic, cigarettes, magazines and a lunch counter where students argue about Freud and Mencken over coffee cabinets.

places.name: The Commons Beanery
places.summary: A basement lunch room of long tables where students and junior faculty eat baked beans, brown bread and hash at prices made for scholarships.

places.name: Haskett boathouse
places.summary: A shingled boathouse on the river where the crew rows at dawn and anyone with a quarter can hire a canoe on summer evenings.

places.name: Blanchard Observatory
places.summary: A small domed observatory with public nights on clear Fridays, which in Pellmouth are fewer than the astronomers would like.

places.name: Haskett chapel
places.summary: A plain brick chapel with a bell that rings the hours and an organ students practise on at odd times of night.

places.name: St. Jean-Baptiste Church
places.summary: The big brick church of the French-Canadian parish, with sermons in French, a parochial school and a bell that wakes the mill blocks on Sunday.

places.name: The Falls Diner
places.summary: A Worcester lunch car by the mill gate, serving the shifts eggs, hash, pea soup and coffee from five in the morning till midnight.

places.name: Côté's Market
places.summary: A corner grocery of salt pork, molasses, tourtière at Christmas, maple sugar in spring and credit on the slate until payday.

places.name: Club Social Lafayette
places.summary: A members' club over a hardware store with cards, a pool table and near beer on the price list; the real beer is brewed in a cellar two streets over.

places.name: Lafayette Bowling Alleys
places.summary: Eight candlepin lanes with pinsetters, a league every weeknight and the clatter of pins until eleven.

places.name: The falls footbridge
places.summary: An iron footbridge over the falls where mill workers eat lunch in the spray and couples walk after the evening shift.

places.name: St. Brendan's Church
places.summary: The Irish parish church, with a Sunday crowd that spills down the steps and a parish hall that holds whist drives and dances.

places.name: Pellmouth YMCA
places.summary: A brick Y with a swimming tank, a running track over the gym, boxing on Tuesday nights and Bible classes nobody is made to attend.

places.name: O'Day's Lunch Room
places.summary: Corned beef, boiled dinner on Thursdays, fish cakes on Fridays and a counter where the car-barn crews take their dinner.

places.name: First Spiritualist Society hall
places.summary: A plain upstairs hall with folding chairs and a harmonium, where Sunday evening services end with a medium reading messages for whoever came hoping for one.

places.name: Riverside Oval
places.summary: A cinder-ringed ballfield by the river where the Twilight League plays after supper and the high school plays football on Thanksgiving morning.

places.name: The back room at Mahoney's Garage
places.summary: A speakeasy behind a garage where you drink gin out of teacups among tyre racks, and a fiddler and a banjo play reels and foxtrots by turns.

places.name: Hibernian Hall
places.summary: A dance hall over a block of shops with Saturday dances, a St. Patrick's ball and a polished floor the young people wear thin.

places.name: Kelleher's Market
places.summary: A corner grocery and meat market with sawdust on the floor, corned beef in the barrel and the week's gossip at the register.

places.name: State Hospital grounds
places.summary: The long brick wings and central tower of Pellmouth State Hospital, set in lawns behind an iron fence; families walk there on visiting Sundays, and townsfolk lower their voices driving past.

places.name: Bluff cliff walk
places.summary: A path along the cliff above the rocks with the whole harbor mouth below, the light on the point opposite and the fog coming in like a wall.

places.name: Hospital Road Inn
places.summary: A plain inn by the hospital gate for families come to visit, with a dining room of pot roast and pie and a landlord who never asks whom you have come to see.

places.name: Ellery's general store
places.summary: Groceries, tobacco, postcards and the post office in one, kept by a family who have sold to hospital staff for forty years.

places.name: State Hospital farm and greenhouses
places.summary: Fields, a dairy and glasshouses worked by patients and attendants; the greenhouse sells cut flowers and seedlings at the gate.

places.name: The Lacey parlour
places.summary: A front parlour in a staff cottage where a medium holds private sittings by lamplight, with tea after and a donation jar on the hall table.

places.name: Gannet Point Light
places.summary: A white stone tower and keeper's house on the rocks at the harbor mouth. The lamp is lit at sunset by the almanac, and sometimes well before it, which the keeper puts down to the fog.

places.name: Long Sands beach
places.summary: A mile of sand inside the point with bathhouses, cold water, picnics in July and a bonfire on the Fourth.

places.name: Gannet Point Pavilion
places.summary: A summer dance pavilion on pilings with a bandstand, Japanese lanterns and dance tickets at a dime; it shuts after the Harvest Moon dance.

places.name: Pike's Clam Shack
places.summary: A shack on the causeway frying clams in lard and selling them in paper boats with a pickle, from Decoration Day to Labor Day.

places.name: The Gannet House
places.summary: A shingled inn that stays open all year, with a parlour fire, fish dinners, and a ledger of guests going back to 1868 that the proprietor likes to read aloud from.

places.name: The Ledges
places.summary: Flat granite ledges below the lighthouse full of tide pools, where children hunt crabs and the old people say not to stay past the turn.

places.name: Gannet Point Coast Guard station
places.summary: A shingled lifeboat station with a lookout tower and a wireless mast, where the crew drills on the beach every morning and watches for rum-runners every night.

places.name: Number Four quarry
places.summary: A granite pit abandoned in 1908 when it struck a spring and flooded overnight; the water is black and very still, and the company has fenced it twice.

places.name: The Deep Hole
places.summary: An old pit with a granite ledge to jump from, where young people swim in summer despite the signs and the stories.

places.name: Zanetti's
places.summary: A front-room restaurant of spaghetti, veal and bread, with red wine served in coffee cups and accordion music on Saturdays.

places.name: Quarry Workers' Cooperative Store
places.summary: A cooperative store run by the Finnish and Italian families, with flour, olive oil, rye bread, dried fish and a share for every member.

places.name: Società di Mutuo Soccorso hall
places.summary: The Italian mutual-aid society's hall, with bocce out back, a bar that sells only coffee and anisette, and dances on feast days.

places.name: Polish National Home
places.summary: A hall with a long bar, kielbasa and pickles, a polka band on Saturdays and a choir practising upstairs on Wednesdays.

places.name: St. Casimir's Church
places.summary: A wooden Polish church the quarry families built themselves on Sundays, with a painted ceiling and a choir that can be heard from the pits.

places.name: Pratt's Pond
places.summary: A spring-fed pond ringed by pines where families picnic in summer, with a warming hut for skaters and a willow children dare each other to climb.

places.name: Skating on Pratt's Pond
places.summary: The whole town skates on Pratt's Pond once the selectmen hang out the red ball, with a bonfire, hot cider and a hockey game at one end.

places.name: Sayer's Rock
places.summary: A split boulder in a hayfield where, the story goes, the widow Annis Sayer was examined in 1692 and from which she was never seen to come down. Nothing grows in the crack, and the farmer mows around it.

places.name: Dodge's cider mill
places.summary: A press barn of sweet cider, doughnuts, apples by the peck and jugs of hard cider sold to people the family knows.

places.name: West Parish Grange Hall
places.summary: A plain hall of bean suppers, contra dances with a fiddler caller, and the Harvest Moon dance in October.

places.name: The Wayside
places.summary: A roadhouse on the Boston road with chicken dinners, a dance floor and a back room where the cider is applejack; the motorcar crowd drives out from town on Saturday nights.

careers.name: Asylum attendant
careers.summary: Twelve-hour shifts on the wards of the State Hospital: bathing, feeding and watching patients, walking them on the lawns, and living in the attendants' home.

careers.name: Lighthouse keeper
careers.summary: Keeping the Gannet Point lamp lit, the lens polished, the fog bell rung and the log written up, through every watch of the night.

careers.name: Rare-books cataloguer
careers.summary: Cataloguing the Whitcomb bequest card by card at the Lindall Library, in a room that must be locked at sundown.

careers.name: Tide-table clerk
careers.summary: Working out and posting the week's tides, keeping the harbormaster's ledgers and logging every vessel in and out.

careers.name: Fish-cannery hand
careers.summary: Gutting, packing and sealing fish at the Pell River Packing Company, on shifts set by whatever the boats bring in.

careers.name: Séance medium
careers.summary: Holding sittings in a front parlour and reading messages at the Spiritualist hall for people who have lost someone.

careers.name: Dowser
careers.summary: Walking farms and house lots with a forked witch-hazel stick to find where a well should go, paid if the water comes.

careers.name: Quarry worker
careers.summary: Drilling, blasting and splitting granite in the Pellmouth Granite Company pits, by derrick and steam drill.

careers.name: Sexton
careers.summary: Ringing the bell, minding the furnace, keeping the burying ground and digging the graves for First Parish.

careers.name: Folklore lecturer
careers.summary: Teaching New England folklore at Haskett and collecting ballads, sayings and stories from old people who would rather not be written down.

careers.name: Wireless operator
careers.summary: Keeping the night watch on the Coast Guard station's wireless set, and a radio ham in the off hours who talks to strangers across the ocean.

careers.name: Clam digger
careers.summary: Digging soft-shell clams on the flats at low tide with a fork and a hod, and selling them to the clam shacks and the cannery.

careers.name: Boatbuilder
careers.summary: Building and mending dories and draggers at Ellsworth's yard by eye, adze and steam box.

careers.name: Ferry deckhand
careers.summary: Handling lines, fares and the gangway on the Pell River ferry, and telling the skipper when the fog is too thick to cross.

employers.name: Haskett University
employers.summary: A small old university of six hundred students, a library with a famous and peculiar bequest, a museum and an observatory.

employers.name: Pellmouth State Normal School
employers.summary: The state teachers' college and its model school, training schoolteachers for the North Shore.

employers.name: Pellmouth State Hospital
employers.summary: The state hospital for the insane on the bluff, with fourteen hundred patients, its own farm, laundry and power house, and the largest payroll in town.

employers.name: Gannet Point Light and Coast Guard station
employers.summary: The lighthouse, its keepers and the Coast Guard lifeboat station beside it, which also keeps a lookout for rum-runners.

employers.name: Harbormaster's office
employers.summary: The harbormaster and clerks in the Old Custom House, keeping moorings, tides and the vessel log.

employers.name: Pell River Packing Company
employers.summary: The cannery on the wharf, packing sardines, fish flakes and chowder clams for grocers across New England.

employers.name: Narrows Fishermen's Cooperative
employers.summary: The Narrows families' co-op of boats, nets, ice house and fish stalls.

employers.name: Ellsworth's boatyard
employers.summary: A family boatyard building dories and fishing draggers.

employers.name: Pellmouth Granite Company
employers.summary: The granite company working four pits west of town for paving blocks, curbstone and monuments.

employers.name: Hatch & Merrill Shoe Company
employers.summary: Two brick shoe mills at the falls making work boots and women's shoes, on piece rates.

employers.name: Pellmouth Evening Courier
employers.summary: The town's evening paper: shipping news, tide tables, court reports and the social column.

employers.name: Tibbetts & Son Funeral Home
employers.summary: The old funeral parlour in a gambrel house on Church Street, three generations in the trade.

employers.name: First Parish Church
employers.summary: The Unitarian church of the old families, and keeper of the Old Hill Burying Ground.

employers.name: First Spiritualist Society
employers.summary: A Spiritualist congregation with an upstairs hall, Sunday message services and mediums who also sit privately for a fee.

employers.name: Pellmouth & Shore Street Railway
employers.summary: The trolley company and its car barn.

employers.name: Pellmouth Police Department
employers.summary: Two dozen officers working out of the town hall basement, more busy with fog than with crime.

employers.name: Pellmouth telephone exchange
employers.summary: The switchboard over the bank where every call in town goes through a pair of hands.

career_hubs.name: The waterfront
career_hubs.summary: Wharves, the cannery, the boatyard, the ferry, the light and every boat in the harbor, including the ones that come in without lights.

career_hubs.name: The hill and the square
career_hubs.summary: The university, the State Hospital, the churches, the bank, the paper and the shops.

career_hubs.name: The mills and the pits
career_hubs.summary: The shoe mills at the falls, the granite pits, the car barn and the farms up the river.

climate.summary: The North Shore coast: cold snowy winters with nor'easters, a raw late spring, fog banks off the water from May to July, warm summers cooled by the sea breeze, and a clear, bright autumn.

months.note: Cold and gray; nor'easters bring snow and tides over the wharves.
Snow on the ground, ice in the river; the winter carnival.
Raw and windy, with the worst of the nor'easters.
Cold rain, mud and the first fog banks.
Lilacs on the hill; fog most mornings until noon.
Sea fog rolls in at evening; the fog horn sounds half the night.
Warm days, sea breeze, and fog that comes and goes in an hour.
The warmest water of the year; thunderstorms over the flats.
Clear and golden; a gale now and then.
Bright leaves, frost in West Parish, the Harvest Moon.
Gray and blowing; nor'easter season begins.
Short dark days, first snow, ice creeping out on the pond.

annual_events.name: Haskett Winter Carnival
annual_events.summary: A weekend of ski jumping off the observatory hill, snow sculptures in the Old Yard, a torchlight skate and the Carnival Ball.

annual_events.name: Haskett commencement
annual_events.summary: Caps and gowns in the Old Yard, the chapel bell, class day picnics and parents filling every room in town.

annual_events.name: Blessing of the Fleet
annual_events.summary: The priest of the Holy Ghost blesses every boat from the end of the landing, the boats circle the harbor dressed in flags, and the Narrows holds open house for an afternoon.

annual_events.name: Founders' Day
annual_events.summary: The town's birthday, kept since 1843: a parade of the militia, fire companies and schools, an oration on the common and a band concert.

annual_events.name: Feast of the Holy Ghost
annual_events.summary: The Narrows' festa: a crowning in the church, a procession, and free sopas of beef and bread for everyone, strangers included.

annual_events.name: The Fourth
annual_events.summary: Bells at dawn, the parade through Market Square, a band at the pavilion and a bonfire on Long Sands.

annual_events.name: The night of the lights on the river
annual_events.summary: On the night of the lowest August tide the Narrows floats candles in paper boats down the river from the tide steps, for the drowned. The rest of town comes to watch; nobody explains why it must be that night.

annual_events.name: The last night of September
annual_events.summary: The anniversary of the widow Sayer's examination, which the town does not mark: shops close early, curtains are drawn, the Historical Society shuts at noon, and nobody is in the hayfield after dark.

annual_events.name: Harvest Moon dance
annual_events.summary: The grange hall's big dance of the year under paper lanterns, with a fiddler caller, cider and a supper of baked beans and pie.

annual_events.name: Armistice Day
annual_events.summary: Silence at eleven at the war memorial, the Legion parade, and names of the Pellmouth dead read out from the town hall steps.

annual_events.name: First ice on Pratt's Pond
annual_events.summary: The day the selectmen declare the ice safe and hang out the red ball, half the town skips work to skate.

local_color.name: "Mind the tide"
local_color.summary: The Narrows' way of saying goodbye, and also of saying mind your own business; strangers rarely know which is meant.

local_color.name: "Gone up the Bluff"
local_color.summary: Said of someone committed to the State Hospital, in a low voice, and never in front of the family.

local_color.name: "The light's early"
local_color.summary: Said when the Gannet Point lamp is lit before sunset: the boats stay in, parents call the children home, and the Courier blames the fog.

local_color.name: "Wicked"
local_color.summary: The North Shore's all-purpose intensifier: wicked cold, wicked good, a wicked lot of fog.

local_color.name: Lamps on the spring tides
local_color.summary: In the Narrows a lamp burns in every window that faces the river on the nights of the big spring tides. Ask why and you are told it always has.

local_color.name: No whistling on the wharf
local_color.summary: Nobody whistles on a Pellmouth wharf or aboard a boat; it calls up wind, or worse, and a newcomer who does it is told once.

local_color.name: Out of the Whitcomb Room by sundown
local_color.summary: By the terms of the bequest the Whitcomb Room is locked at sundown, and the librarians clear it ten minutes early, every day, without exception.

local_color.name: Saturday beans
local_color.summary: Baked beans with salt pork and molasses and steamed brown bread for Saturday supper, in nearly every kitchen in town.

local_color.name: Fish chowder
local_color.summary: Haddock, potatoes, salt pork and milk, never tomatoes; arguing about the crackers is allowed.

local_color.name: Fried clams
local_color.summary: Whole-belly clams fried in lard in a paper boat, a summer thing from the shacks on the causeway.

local_color.name: Kale soup
local_color.summary: The Narrows' soup of kale, potatoes, beans and linguiça, on the stove all winter.

local_color.name: Tourtière
local_color.summary: Spiced pork pie the Falls families bake for Christmas Eve after midnight mass.

local_color.name: A frappe
local_color.summary: Ice cream shaken with milk and syrup; in Pellmouth a milkshake has no ice cream in it, and visitors find out the hard way.

local_color.name: Canadian
local_color.summary: Whisky that came down from Nova Scotia on a schooner and in over the flats on a foggy night; the town calls it simply "Canadian".

local_color.name: West Parish hard cider
local_color.summary: Cider left to work in the barrel over the winter, legal if you made it yourself and sold by the jug to people the family knows.

local_color.name: The Twilight League
local_color.summary: Mill, car barn, cannery and quarry teams playing seven innings after supper at Riverside Oval, with bets the whole town knows about.

local_color.name: The Haskett crew
local_color.summary: The university eight, who row the river at dawn and lose to bigger colleges every spring with great dignity.

local_color.name: The widow Sayer
local_color.summary: Annis Sayer, a widow of West Parish, was examined for witchcraft on a boulder in 1692. The court papers stop mid-page; the story says she was never seen to come down.

local_color.name: The sealed meetinghouse
local_color.summary: The Second Parish meetinghouse was shut in 1894 after a winter service nobody who attended would describe. The record says a quarrel and a bad roof.

local_color.name: Number Four has no bottom
local_color.summary: Quarry Village says nobody has ever sounded the bottom of Number Four, that the water is warm in January, and that what goes in does not come up.

local_color.name: The Narrows know the tide
local_color.summary: Uptown it is said the Narrows families know the tides better than the printed tables, and that on some nights they go down to the steps to meet it. The Narrows says uptown talks too much.

local_color.name: What is in the Whitcomb Room
local_color.summary: Students swear one of the Whitcomb journals is written in no known language, and that a professor who asked to take it home left the faculty the same term.

local_color.name: The fourth floor of the tower
local_color.summary: Attendants say nobody is ever assigned to the top floor of the State Hospital tower, and that its lights are on all the same.

local_color.name: The spa
local_color.summary: A Massachusetts "spa" is a corner store with a soda fountain, tobacco and magazines; the College Spa on College Hill is the one everybody means.

local_color.name: Tuttle's back room
local_color.summary: The antiquarian bookshop keeps its oldest stock in a back room shown only to customers it knows, which is most of what anyone talks about.

prices.per: a dozen on the half shell
a day in the mills, the pits or the cannery; clerks $20-$30 a week

quirks.text: keeps the tide table pinned by the door
quirks.bio: I know when high water is. Always.

quirks.text: won't whistle near the water after dark
quirks.bio: I will not whistle by the harbor after dark. Do not ask me why; nobody here does.

quirks.text: counts the foghorn blasts under their breath
quirks.bio: I count the foghorn. It passes the time.

quirks.text: always takes the long way round the old meetinghouse
quirks.bio: I take the long way round the old meetinghouse. Habit.

quirks.text: reads the Courier shipping news before the front page
quirks.bio: Shipping news first, then the rest of the paper.

quirks.text: keeps a lamp lit in the window on foggy nights
quirks.bio: There is always a lamp in my window when the fog comes in.

quirks.text: taps the barometer every time they pass a chandlery window
quirks.bio: I tap every barometer I pass. Old skipper habit, and I never was a skipper.

quirks.text: knows every family plot in the Old Hill Burying Ground
quirks.bio: Ask me about anyone in the Old Hill Burying Ground.

goals.text: build a dory of their own over the winter
goals.progress: {name} got another strake fastened on the dory in the shed
goals.done: {name} launched the new dory off the town landing, with half the street watching
goals.bio: Building a dory in my shed, one plank at a time.

goals.text: trace their family back through the town's old records
goals.progress: {name} found another great-grandparent in the Athenaeum ledgers
goals.done: {name} traced the family back to the first settlers, and stopped there
goals.bio: Digging through the town records for my family.

goals.text: win the chowder supper at the West Parish Grange
goals.progress: {name} tried another batch of chowder on the neighbors
goals.done: {name} took first prize for chowder, and will not share the secret
goals.bio: Working on a chowder that will win the Grange supper.

goals.text: save for a mooring and a boat in the harbor
goals.progress: {name} put another week of pay towards a mooring
goals.done: {name} has a boat on a mooring of their own at last
goals.bio: Saving for a mooring in the harbor.

goals.text: get a place in Boston and off the North Shore
goals.progress: {name} wrote off to another Boston firm about a position
goals.done: {name} got an offer in Boston, and has not yet said whether they will go
goals.bio: Looking for a job in Boston. Maybe.
